At least 50% of the portfolio must be loans of up to ₹25 lakh, applied borrower-wise. What is the position?

options.text: Borrowers A, C and E qualify (₹64 lakh of ₹124 lakh, about 51.6%), so the norm is met
All loans except B's qualify (₹94 lakh, about 75.8%)
Only C and E qualify (₹44 lakh, about 35.5%), so it fails
Every loan is below ₹25 lakh except B's, so the share is 100% less B

solution.explanation: The ₹25 lakh limit is borrower-wise, and the whole portfolio counts. Borrower totals: A 20, B 30, C 20, D 30, E 24. Qualifying: A, C, E = 64 of 124 ≈ 51.6% ≥ 50%. D's three loans of 10 each total 30 and do not qualify.
steps: Totals: A 20, B 30, C 20, D 30, E 24
solution.why_others_wrong: Counting D loan-by-loan ignores the borrower-wise rule; excluding A also misapplies it.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Borrowers A, C and E qualify (₹64 lakh of ₹124 lakh, about 51.6%), so the norm is met

I. It may make the buyback offer from 8 December 2026, seven days after issue.

Claims up to ₹60 crore (1.5 times) are settled; ₹35 crore is rejected
Claims up to ₹80 crore are settled; ₹15 crore of claims are kept suspended until the payout is within the cap

Immediately on 15 November 2026; within 3 years, i.e. by 15 November 2029
From 20 October 2026, after a 9-month lock-in; by 20 October 2029
From 15 November 2027, one year after NPA; by 15 November 2028
